chapter_text_kjv.12: And whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.
chapter_text_kjv.13: But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in.
chapter_text_kjv.14: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows’ houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation.
chapter_text_kjv.15: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.
chapter_text_kjv.16: Woe unto you, ye blind guides, which say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor!
chapter_text_kjv.17: Ye fools and blind: for whether is greater, the gold, or the temple that sanctifieth the gold?
chapter_text_kjv.18: And, Whosoever shall swear by the altar, it is nothing; but whosoever sweareth by the gift that is upon it, he is guilty.
chapter_text_kjv.19: Ye fools and blind: for whether is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifieth the gift?

chapter_text_kjv.21: And whoso shall swear by the temple, sweareth by it, and by him that dwelleth therein.
chapter_text_kjv.22: And he that shall swear by heaven, sweareth by the throne of Elohim (God), and by him that sitteth thereon.
chapter_text_kjv.23: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.
chapter_text_kjv.24: Ye blind guides, which strain at a gnat, and swallow a camel.
chapter_text_kjv.25: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess.

chapter_text_kjv.27: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness.
chapter_text_kjv.28: Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.

chapter_text_kjv.30: And say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.
chapter_text_kjv.31: Wherefore ye be witnesses unto yourselves, that ye are the children of them which killed the prophets.
chapter_text_kjv.32: Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers.
chapter_text_kjv.33: Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?
chapter_text_kjv.34: Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city:

chapter_text_kjv.36: Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation.
chapter_text_kjv.37: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!
chapter_text_kjv.38: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.
chapter_text_kjv.39: For I say unto you, Ye shall not see me henceforth, till ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of Yahuah (Lord).

threads.summary_md: Matt 23:1-12's introduction — *the scribes and the Pharisees sit in Mosheh's (Moses's) seat* + *they say, and do not* + the heavy-burdens-the-leadership-substance-binds-on-others-while-not-moving-them-with-one-finger + the for-to-be-seen-of-men display of broadened-Tefillin and enlarged-Tsitsit (the *making-broad* and *enlarging* of the Torah-substance for the display, NOT the Tefillin or Tsitsit themselves — the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walked-the-Tsitsit himself per Matt 9:20 and 14:36) + the love-of-uppermost-rooms-at-feasts-and-chief-seats-in-the-synagogues + the categorical-rejection-of-religious-paternity-titles (NOT against the Hebrew-teaching-relationship the apostles still walked or the natural-father-honor the King walked at the cross at John 19:26-27, but against the substance-of-religious-status the leadership-substance loved) + the kingdom-inversion-substance (*he that is greatest among you shall be your servant*) — read against the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the pride-and-religious-status architecture in Sirach (Ecclesiasticus). threads.title: The corrupted priesthood and the proselyte made twofold — Testament of Levi, 1 Enoch 99, Wisdom of Solomon beside Matthew 23:13-22
threads.summary_md: The first three woes are aimed at a priesthood. They shut up the kingdom of heaven against men and will not go in themselves, they split hairs over which oath binds and which does not, and in between those two stands the woe that names what the whole system was doing: *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.* (Matthew 23:15). The proselyte was told that becoming a Yahudi (Jew) by the rite would save him, and then he was handed a Torah buried under traditions that voided it, so he ended up worse off than the men who made him. Paul fights the same gospel in Galatia a generation later, and it is still being preached today under other names, wherever a system tells a man that joining it is salvation and then teaches him against the commandments. Enoch had already described the men who do this: *Woe to them who pervert the words of uprightness, And transgress the eternal law, And transform themselves into what they were not [into sinners]: They shall be trodden under foot upon the earth.* (1 Enoch 99:2). Perverting the words of uprightness while transgressing the eternal law is the proselyte-maker's trade exactly, and the man he makes is transformed into what he was not. The Testament of Levi had warned the priests themselves that they would deal lawlessly with Yashar'el (Israel) until the veil of the temple was rent, and that the priests of the last times would be idolaters, adulterers, lovers of money, proud and lawless, and the Wisdom of Solomon tells the ministers of the kingdom that they will be judged because they did not judge aright nor keep the law. The test is the same one John gives: whoever says he knows him and does not keep his commandments is a liar. Hold that against any priesthood, in any age, and the woes find their mark. The mark is the system, not the people under it. The King speaking the woes is himself a Yahudi (Jew), so are the apostles, so are the crowds in front of him, and the chapter ends not with their rejection but with his lament over the children he would have gathered.

threads.title: The blood of Hevel (Abel) crying and the mother hen gathering — 1 Enoch 22 and 2 Esdras 1 beside Matthew 23:29-39
threads.summary_md: The seventh woe ends with blood. *That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zechariah son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.* (Matthew 23:35). Yahusha (Jesus) reaches back to the first murder and forward to the last one recorded in the Hebrew order of the books, and lays the whole line of slain prophets at the feet of the men who were building the prophets' tombs. The ground had been crying the whole time: *And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground.* (Genesis 4:10). Enoch was shown where that cry goes. In the mountain in the west, among the hollow places where the souls of the dead wait for the day of judgement, one voice goes up louder than the rest: *I saw the spirits of the children of men who were dead, and their voice went forth to heaven and made suit. Then I asked Raphael the angel who was with me, and I said unto him: 'This spirit—whose is it, whose voice goeth forth and maketh suit?' And he answered me saying: 'This is the spirit which went forth from Abel, whom his brother Cain slew, and he makes his suit against him till his seed is destroyed from the face of the earth, and his seed is annihilated from amongst the seed of men.'* (1 Enoch 22:5-7). Abel is still making his suit, and it is a suit against a seed, not against one man. That is why the woe is addressed to *Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?* (Matthew 23:33). The men who killed the prophets and were about to kill the Son are the seed Abel's blood has been pleading against since the field outside Eden, sown in among the people and wearing the priest's robe, and the judgement that falls on them is not a judgement on the Yahudim (Jews) as a people. The same chapter of Enoch shows the hollow places divided, the righteous by their spring of water, the sinners kept for the great day, and those who were slain making their disclosure against the ones who slew them, so the damnation of Gehenna the woe names is a holding and a judgement, not the endless torture the pulpit painted over it. Then the voice changes. *O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!* (Matthew 23:37). Ezra had heard the Father say the same thing in the same words, that he gathered them as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings, that he sent them prophets whom they took and slew, and that their house is desolate (2 Esdras 1:30-33). The Son speaks with the Father's own voice and the Father's own grief. The judgement on the shepherds is what clears the ground for the gathering, as Ezekiel 34 lays it out, and the lament is not a door shut on the city. It is the Father's heart toward the children of the broken-off, who will yet be brought home out of the nations the way the prophets said they would be.

Enoch was shown the prison of the angels and told it holds them for ever. The judgment the serpents cannot escape is the judgment their fathers, the Watchers, are already held for; the seed goes where the seed came from.

The Pharisaic system voids Torah by addition (the fences) and by subtraction (the heart). The framework-major diagnostic of the Judaizer Error is operating in front of the reader: the system that wears Torah's robes and builds a parallel Torah on top that contradicts the original.

For Elohim (God) commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother ... But ye say, Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, It is a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free. The King's-charge at vv.3-6 lands at the same load-bearing diagnostic the wisdom-stream had named: the disposition that voids the parental-honor commandment is at the architecture of blasphemy-against-the-Torah-the-Father-spoke-from-Sinai.

threads.title: Out of the heart proceed evil thoughts — to eat with unwashen hands defileth not (Genesis 6; Jeremiah 17; Psalm 51; Proverbs 4; Mark 7)
threads.summary_md: Hear carefully what is — and is NOT — being said. The question on the table is hand-washing: *they wash not their hands when they eat bread* (15:2), and the saying closes on exactly that point: *these are the things which defile a man: but to eat with unwashen hands defileth not a man* (15:20). This is the Pharisees' ritual tradition, not the clean and unclean foods of Leviticus 11 and Deuteronomy 14, which stand unmoved. The subject is moral defilement versus a ceremonial rinse. *Not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man* — and the source is the heart, just as the Tanakh has always taught. *And GOD saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually* (Genesis 6:5) — the heart's evil imagination that brought the flood is the true uncleanness. *The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it?* (Jeremiah 17:9). David knew where Elohim looks: *Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts: and in the hidden part thou shalt make me to know wisdom* (Psalm 51:6) — *create in me a clean heart, O Elohim.* And the wisdom of Proverbs is the very key to the parable: *Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life* (Proverbs 4:23) — out of the heart flow the things that defile. Mark teaches the identical lesson with the identical setting: *That which cometh out of the man, that defileth the man. For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts* (Mark 7:20-21), the answer to those who *eat bread with unwashen hands.* Guard this well: it is not the dietary law repealed — it is the heart unmasked, the hand-washing tradition put in its place.

threads.title: Peace, and there was no peace — the wall daubed with untempered morter shall fall
threads.summary_md: The lie of the false prophets takes a shape: a wall whitewashed to look sound. *Because, even because they have seduced my people, saying, Peace; and there was no peace; and one built up a wall, and, lo, others daubed it with untempered morter* (13:10). The daubing is the false comfort smeared over a breach that was never repaired. Yahuah will test it with the storm: *there shall be an overflowing shower; and ye, O great hailstones, shall fall; and a stormy wind shall rend it* (13:11), *So will I break down the wall that ye have daubed with untempered morter, and bring it down to the ground, so that the foundation thereof shall be discovered, and it shall fall* (13:14) — and the verdict on the peace-prophets: *the prophets of Yashar'el (Israel) which prophesy concerning Jerusalem, and which see visions of peace for her, and there is no peace* (13:16). Jeremiah cries the very lie twice — *saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace* (Jeremiah 6:14; Jeremiah 8:11) — the slight healing that covers the wound without closing it. Paul names where the false peace ends: *when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them, as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape* (1 Thessalonians 5:3). The Formed Son draws the same collapsing structure as the house on sand: *every one that heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, which built his house upon the sand: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell: and great was the fall of it* (Matthew 7:26-27) — the storm that rends the daubed wall and the storm that beats down the sand-built house are one. And Paul names a man to his face with Ezekiel's image: *Elohim (God) shall smite thee, thou whited wall* (Acts 23:3) — fair without, hollow within. Untempered morter and a false *Peace*: a wall built to fall.

threads.title: Save now (Hosanna) — Blessed be he that cometh in the name of Yahuah
threads.summary_md: *Save now, I beseech thee, O Yahuah (LORD): O Yahuah (LORD), I beseech thee, send now prosperity. Blessed be he that cometh in the name of Yahuah (LORD): we have blessed you out of the house of Yahuah (LORD)* (Psalm 118:25-26). *Save now* is the Hosanna — the very plea in the tongue of the people. This is the climax of the Hallel sung at every Passover, and the day came when the crowds sang it over the One entering Jerusalem: *Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of Yahuah (Lord); Hosanna in the highest* (Matthew 21:9); *Hosanna; Blessed is he that cometh in the name of Yahuah (Lord)* (Mark 11:9); *Blessed be the King that cometh in the name of Yahuah (Lord)* (Luke 19:38); and with palm branches, *Blessed is the King of Yashar'el (Israel) that cometh in the name of Yahuah (Lord)* (John 12:13). The feast-cry of the Hallel is placed on the One who comes — *he that cometh in the name of Yahuah* has come, the King of Yashar'el (Israel) riding into his city, and the people's *Save now* is the prayer the comer answers.

members_elsewhere_sample.member_note: *Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of Yahuah (Lord); Hosanna in the highest* (Matthew 21:9) — *Save now* (118:25) IS the Hosanna; the crowds sing the Hallel over Yahusha entering Jerusalem.

threads.title: As a hen gathereth her chickens; your house desolate
threads.summary_md: The lament turns tender before it turns to judgment: *I gathered you together, as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings: but now, what shall I do to you? I will cast you out from my face* (2 Esdras 1:30), and the sentence, *Your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind does stubble* (2 Esdras 1:33). It ain't new — Yahusha stands over the same Jerusalem and weeps the same figure word for word: *O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!* (Matthew 23:37), and pronounces the same desolation, *Behold, your house is left unto you desolate* (Matthew 23:38). The grief is the grief of a Father, not the spite of a stranger — the same yearning hand, the same withdrawn house, in the mouth of the Messiah.

members_elsewhere_sample.member_note: Matthew 23:37 — *O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!* Yahusha takes up the hen-and-chickens figure of 2 Esdras 1:30 exactly — the same yearning, the same refusal.
Matthew 23:38 — *Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.* The desolate house of 2 Esdras 1:33 is the very word Yahusha speaks over Jerusalem — the house given over.
